results.title: Real-World Data: What Is It and Why Does It Matter?
results.content: Real-world data is critical to clinical research, drug development, and patient insights for better outcomes. By using sources of patient health data, researchers can evaluate therapies in a larger population, in real-world conditions, and at a lower cost than with typical clinical trials. ‍Healthcare providers can use RWD and RWE to better inform a patient’s treatment plan, procedures, tests, and prescriptions, and these data may help develop practice guidelines. As patients move throughout the health system, valuable real-world data is collected as part of their electronic health records (EHRs). To gain a comprehensive understanding of patient health, a recent trend in healthcare is to link proprietary pharma company data—such as clinical trials, aggregated specialty drug data, and disease or device registries—with real-world data offered by commercial data providers. For life sciences organizations, medical record retrieval unlocks the “last mile” of real-world data (RWD) – providing access to complete, patient-level records that fill gaps left by traditional sources.
